topics.title: Fourier series
topics.essence: Any periodic signal is a sum of phasors spinning at whole multiples of one fundamental frequency.
topics.check: You make a square wave's period twice as long. What happens to the spacing of its harmonics on the frequency axis?

topics.title: discrete-time Fourier series
topics.essence: A sequence that repeats every N samples is a sum of exactly N phasors e^(j2πkn/N), for k = 0 to N − 1. N numbers in time become N numbers in frequency, and nothing is lost.
topics.check: A sequence has period 4. How many distinct harmonics does it have, and why are there no more?

topics.title: DFT
topics.essence: The DFT is that same change of basis applied to any N samples, written as an N by N matrix whose columns are orthogonal phasors. Its inverse is its conjugate transpose, up to a constant.
topics.check: Why is the inverse of the DFT matrix so easy to write down?

later.how: The DFT and the FFT are the working tools for measuring spectra and for fast filtering.

topics.title: FFT
topics.essence: The FFT computes the DFT by splitting the samples into even and odd halves, again and again. The work drops from N² operations to N log₂ N.
topics.check: For N = 1024, roughly how many times less work is the FFT than the direct sum?

topics.title: symmetry and shifts in Fourier series
topics.essence: The look of a signal in time fixes the pattern of its coefficients. A real signal has conjugate-symmetric coefficients, a real even signal has real ones, and a time shift only turns each coefficient's phase.
topics.check: A real periodic signal is shifted by half a period. What happens to the magnitude and to the phase of its kth coefficient?

topics.title: Parseval's relation
topics.essence: The energy of a signal added up over time equals its energy added up over frequency. Changing to an orthogonal basis does not change a vector's length.
topics.check: A periodic signal has only two non-zero Fourier coefficients, of magnitudes 3 and 4. What is its average power?

topics.title: Fourier transform
topics.essence: Let the period grow without limit and the harmonics crowd together into a continuum. X(jω) says how much of the phasor e^(jωt) the signal contains, per unit of frequency.
topics.check: A pulse is made narrower. Before any calculation, what must happen to its transform?

later.how: Filter design is done on the frequency axis, then carried back to time.

topics.title: DTFT
topics.essence: The DTFT is the spectrum of a sequence. It always repeats every 2π in ω, because a sequence cannot tell ω from ω + 2π.
topics.check: x[n] is 1 at n = 0 and at n = 1, and zero elsewhere. Between −π and π, where is |X| largest and where is it zero?

topics.title: time shift is a phase ramp
topics.essence: Delay a signal and the magnitude of its transform does not change. Each frequency's phase turns by −ωt₀, a straight line in ω.
topics.check: Two signals have the same |X(jω)| and different phases. What is the simplest way they can differ in time?

topics.title: frequency shift
topics.essence: Multiply a signal by e^(jω₀t) and its whole spectrum slides to ω₀. Multiplying by a cosine makes two half-size copies, at +ω₀ and −ω₀.
topics.check: A signal whose spectrum is 1 kHz wide about zero is multiplied by a 10 kHz cosine. Where is its spectrum now?

topics.title: convolution becomes multiplication
topics.essence: Convolution in time is multiplication in frequency. That is why filtering is simple in frequency: the output spectrum is the input spectrum times H.
topics.check: A signal goes through the same filter twice. What happens to its spectrum?

topics.title: multiplication becomes convolution
topics.essence: Multiplication in time is convolution in frequency. Cutting a signal off with a window smears its spectrum by the window's transform.
topics.check: A pure tone is observed for only 10 ms. Why is its measured spectrum not a single line, and roughly how wide is it?

topics.title: duality
topics.essence: The transform and its inverse have the same form, so every pair works both ways. A rectangle in time is a sinc in frequency, and a sinc in time is a rectangle in frequency.
topics.check: The transform of a rectangle is a sinc. What is the transform of a sinc, and which familiar system has that frequency response?

topics.title: time and bandwidth trade off
topics.essence: Squeeze a signal in time and its spectrum spreads by the same factor. A signal cannot be short in time and narrow in frequency at once.
topics.check: A pulse is made 10 times shorter. What happens to the bandwidth it needs?

later.how: The rate at which symbols can be sent is limited by the bandwidth of the channel.

topics.title: differentiation in frequency
topics.essence: Differentiating in time multiplies the transform by jω. High frequencies are boosted and a constant is removed.
topics.check: Why does differentiating a noisy measurement make the noise look worse?

topics.title: spectrum of a periodic signal
topics.essence: A periodic signal's transform is a row of impulses at the harmonics, weighted by the Fourier series coefficients. Repeating in time is sampling in frequency.
topics.check: One pulse has a smooth spectrum. The pulse is now repeated every T seconds. What does the spectrum become?

topics.title: impulse train
topics.essence: A row of impulses T apart in time transforms into a row of impulses 2π/T apart in frequency. Pack them closer in time and they move apart in frequency.
topics.check: The impulses are moved twice as close together in time. What happens to the spacing of the lines in frequency?

topics.title: rectangle and sinc
topics.essence: A rectangle of width T has a sinc for its transform, with its first zeros at ±2π/T. The narrower the rectangle, the wider the main lobe.
topics.check: A rectangle is 2 ms wide. At what frequency, in hertz, is the first zero of its transform?

topics.title: windowing and leakage
topics.essence: Looking at a signal through a finite window replaces each spectral line by a copy of the window's transform. Its width blurs nearby tones together, and its side lobes leak energy across the spectrum.
topics.check: Two tones 5 Hz apart are recorded for 0.1 s. Can the spectrum show two peaks? What would you change?

later.how: Choosing a window sets the trade between resolution and leakage in every spectrum estimate.

topics.title: Fourier transform in two dimensions
topics.essence: An image is a sum of two-dimensional waves, each with a direction and a spacing. A point of the 2-D transform far from the centre is fine detail in that direction.
topics.check: An image contains vertical stripes only. Where in the 2-D frequency plane is its transform non-zero?

later.how: A lens forms the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the light in its front focal plane.

links.why: A Fourier coefficient is a projection: how much of the signal lies along one harmonic.
The harmonics are phasors e^(jkω₀t) that make k turns per period.
Only a signal that repeats can be built from whole-number multiples of one frequency.
The N harmonics are orthogonal over one period, so each coefficient is one inner product.
Only a whole number of turns in N steps repeats, which leaves exactly N distinct harmonics.
The DFT is the DTFS of N samples treated as one period.
The even samples and the odd samples each form a DFT of half the size.
Each symmetry of the signal over one period shows up as a pattern in its coefficients.
Because the harmonics are orthogonal, their powers add with no cross terms.
A change to an orthogonal basis keeps inner products, and so keeps energy.
Let the period go to infinity: the spacing between harmonics shrinks to zero and the sum becomes an integral.
Let N grow without limit and the N harmonics fill in the whole interval from −π to π.
A sequence cannot tell ω from ω + 2π, so its spectrum repeats every 2π.
A delay multiplies every phasor e^(jωt) by e^(−jωt₀).
Multiplying by e^(jω₀t) adds ω₀ to the frequency of every phasor in the signal.
Each phasor passes through the convolution scaled by the other signal's transform at that frequency.
An LTI system convolves in time, which multiplies the spectrum by H.
It is the convolution property with the roles of time and frequency exchanged.
Duality turns "convolution in time is multiplication in frequency" round.
The forward and inverse integrals differ only by a sign and a constant.
Compressing the time axis by a stretches the frequency axis by a.
It is what time scaling does to the transform.
Differentiating e^(jωt) brings down a factor of jω.
The rectangle is the first transform worth knowing by heart, and almost every other pair is built from it.
The series coefficients become the weights of impulses at the harmonics.
A periodic signal is one period convolved with an impulse train, so its spectrum is the period's spectrum sampled.
It is the impulse repeated every T seconds.
Multiplying by a window convolves the spectrum with the window's transform.
The simplest window is a rectangle, so each line becomes a sinc.
Taking N samples is windowing, so every DFT shows a smeared spectrum.
The same decomposition, with a wave vector in place of a single frequency.
